conventions.maqaf: A Hebrew prefix letter (ב ה ו כ ל מ ש) before a Latin word, digit or symbol joins it with the Hebrew maqaf U+05BE and no space: ב־GitHub, ה־API, ו־Claude Desktop, מ־3, כ־12%. Never ASCII hyphen-minus or en dash. The same maqaf joins the approved compound פול־סטאק. Transliterated compounds that the owner wrote as one word stay one word (פרונטאנד), so the parallel is בקאנד, not בק־אנד.
conventions.geresh: Use U+05F3 ׳ (not an apostrophe) for transliterated ג׳ צ׳ ז׳ and for abbreviations (דק׳ קריאה); use gershayim U+05F4 ״ inside Hebrew acronyms (ת״י 5568, דוא״ל). Latin acronyms (PR, API, CI, MCP, RSS, URL, JSON) are never transliterated into Hebrew letters with geresh (no פי־אר, איי־פי־איי).
conventions.bidi: Three tools, in order of preference: (1) a whole field that is English gets lang='en' dir='ltr' via inEnglish() (web/src/i18n/words.ts); (2) a multi-token Latin run with punctuation, arrows, colons or version numbers (Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, OAuth 2.1, mcp:read, URLs, key chords) is wrapped in LRI U+2066 … PDI U+2069, as statement.ts mcp.desktop already does; (3) an RLM U+200F goes after a Latin run that is followed by neutral punctuation or a parenthesis (approved: 'Model Context Protocol‏ (MCP)') and at the start of a string that opens with a Latin token or a symbol ('‏claude.ai ו־…', '‏# בוחר נושא'). Do not put RLM inside code identifiers.
conventions.gender: Indeclinable Latin terms take the gender of the Hebrew head noun they stand for, defaulting to masculine: API m (ממשק), MCP m (פרוטוקול/שרת), CI m, PR m (practitioner usage: 'PR ענקיים'), RSS m (פיד), JSON m, README m, webhook m, OAuth m. URL is avoided in favour of כתובת (f). Transliterations: קומיט m, באג m, פיד m, קונטיינר m, פריימוורק m, פרונטאנד/בקאנד m, פול־סטאק adjective (n/a).
conventions.plural_of_latin: Latin tokens are never inflected with Hebrew suffixes (no PRים, APIים, URLים). Number is carried by a numeral, an agreeing adjective or verb ('3 PR פתוחים'), or a Hebrew head noun in construct ('ממשקי API', 'שרתי MCP', 'אסימוני גישה'). Transliterated nouns inflect normally (קומיטים, באגים, פידים, קונטיינרים).

categories.A: Keep Latin script: brand and product names (GitHub, Claude, Docker, React…), protocol/format acronyms and identifiers (API, MCP, CI, RSS, JSON, OAuth, PKCE, URL in code, mcp:read), key names (Enter, Escape, Ctrl+B), standards (WCAG), and tag/slug values. Never transliterate; attach prefixes with maqaf; isolate multi-token runs. A Hebrew word-table entry must still contain Hebrew (words.test KEPT_IN_LATIN is empty), so a Latin term never stands alone as a label.
categories.B: Transliterate in Hebrew letters only when (a) practitioners overwhelmingly use the loan in writing, (b) no Hebrew term is in actual use, and (c) a general reader recognises it: באג, פיד, קונטיינר, פריימוורק, and the owner-approved פול־סטאק / פרונטאנד (+ בקאנד by parallel). Spoken dev slang (קומיט, מרג׳, דיפלוי, ריפו, פוש, טסטים) is NOT promoted to written copy when a transparent Hebrew word exists.
categories.C: Translate to standard Hebrew where an established, widely understood word exists and is used by Israeli UIs (Google, Wix, Microsoft human-reviewed strings) or Hebrew Wikipedia: מאגר, ענף, מיזוג, גרסה, תיעוד, רישיון, קוד פתוח, תוסף, דפדפן, טיוטה, פרסום, תצוגה מקדימה, שרת, נקודת קצה, בדיקות. Reject machine-translation calques (התחייבות, סניף, בקשת משיכה, דחיפה) and Academy coinages the public rejected (מנשק, יישומון).
categories.D: Context-dependent. Public pages describe outcomes in plain Hebrew and avoid the term (push → עדכוני קוד, deploy → השקה, commit/PR omitted). Admin uses the plain Hebrew working term. The /developers/mcp page may use the practitioner term or Latin acronym (PR, קומיט, pipeline, פריסה with object), introduced once as 'Hebrew (English)' with the English isolated.
